The claim states that a zero matrix V is initialized and the corresponding voxel index is set to 1 for each point in P_kappa. Reconstructs a cubic block of voxels at once using a three-pass 3D wavelet reconstruction process, rather than reconstructing each voxel individually, eliminating redundancy [S13, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the three-pass 3D wavelet reconstruction process reconstructs a cubic block of voxels at once by applying 1D wavelet reconstructions along the x, y, and z dimensions sequentially. It further explains that this block-wise approach eliminates the redundancy associated with point-wise (individual voxel) reconstruction, where neighboring voxels would be reconstructed multiple times. The claim accurately reflects these details found in Source [S13].

Classical 3D matrix representation grows as a cube of cells, causing memory issues; the solution is to use a sparse hash table storing only nonzero entries [S14, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that 'the classical representation of a 3D matrix grows as a cube of the number of cells in each dimension' and that this 'poses a problem' (memory issues). It further states that the solution is to use a 'sparse representation' which 'stores only the nonzero entries in a hash table' to avoid the memory problem. This aligns perfectly with the claim.
